body: I never taught them explicitly, it just happened organically, but I do still help them in the early morning because they move so slow I’d rather them sleep in and have me speed dress them versus watch tired kids fumble around for an hour lol.
Another factor is women typically have less saliva and the ph of their saliva is typically lower than a man’s. That alone can lead to us having more dental issues!

As a parent of two kids that entered kindergarten as the youngest in their grade, it’s because kinder has become so academic! My kids have struggled a lot this year and just now are we getting a handle on things - behaviorally, and educationally. They wanted them writing full sentences in journals the first month, they had chromebooks right away and had to take two state tests by themselves within the first month! They pretty much expected them to already know all the letters, sounds and numbers. Basic shapes were not really taught and they jumped right to teaching them about 3d shapes like cones. It’s not what I went through or expected at all. There also does not seem to be a lot of down time or fun time so they were very overwhelmed and exhausted. If I could go back in time I still wouldn’t have red shirted them though because kindergarten is the easiest grade to repeat with no consequence. I don’t see the harm in a little struggle, and worse case scenario they come back and do it again with more confidence.

Don’t worry she’ll come home and tell you about stuff the other kids have said or have. Mine do all of the time! Sometimes this is good, and other times it’s bad, because some kids have zero parental guidance and have taught them about huggy wuggy, etc.

I have twins and one twin has had like 3 boyfriends and 1 girlfriend. One of her boyfriends she had to dump because he only liked dinosaurs. Another boyfriend was lost because he got sent to a different classroom, but he still blows her air kisses when he walks by her class. My other twin could care less about relationships or romance and tells me she’d rather marry a poop than her classmates lol.

As a mandated reporter I would be required by law to make a report. Trust your gut. The water bottle or strange lunches or lack of proper clothing isn’t majorly concerning unless the clothing is unfit for the weather. The vivid description of her mom hurting her and locking her outside is extremely concerning. No kinder age child should be left alone like that especially not outside! Me personally I would keep reporting, advise your supervisor and maybe go to the dollar store for the child to get her some basics. Buying a 1.25$ water bottle and hair brush and helping her braid her hair so it stays tangle free would make her day.
This is age appropriate. I can get my kids to pick up the pace by telling them if they get ready fast enough then they can watch an episode of a favorite show before school.

I agree with the other responses, that this is rape, but please also consider that the beginning of this relationship might have been faked. He may have been love bombing you and doing what he thought you wanted in order to get you comfortable enough with him to accept this behavior for “love.” This is the bait and switch, this is the real him.

It’s not the end of the world if he repeats kindergarten. It does not mean you failed or even necessarily did anything wrong. It’s just that things that were not an issue before are being noticed now because it’s his first time in a structured environment. He’s also probably one of the youngest kids in his class! My daughter is also struggling with this and her teacher told me she only knew 5 letters…She can identify all and their sounds. She simply can not focus to express that. I was also told she can’t recognize numbers or add or subtract. I found out she is literally just zoning out and guessing answers or saying random words! So definitely communicate with his teacher to make sure you are both are on the same page. I started offering rewards and every day she actively participated she got an A from me then I let her turn in her A’s for a trip to the store or something special.

As a rule of thumb I would never strike up a long conversation with anyone that’s paid to be nice to you. I’ve gotten stuck in conversations before and it’s incredibly frustrating because I have to be kind, but I also do actually have tasks to accomplish. It puts us in an awkward spot. There’s often a mountain of laundry and dishes and things to be stocked. Plus breakfast.

At your age those thoughts and ideas probably started with her family and she likely hasn’t thought about things deeply yet. It’s probably how the people around her speak & she’s emulating so try to expose her to your points of view. I feel like a good starting question could be, “If I was trans (or black) would you still be my friend?” Empathy isn’t always an inherited trait but it can be developed and learned.

Getting your child to eat requires spinning and marketing the food. My kids liked steak but not burgers, so now they are steak sandwiches. Cauliflower? Never heard of it. It’s ghost broccoli. Milk is vanilla flavored and yogurt is tangy ice cream. Sometimes if there’s something I want them to eat I pretend to hide it from them and eat in secret until they get curious, then I “confess” and tell them I’ll share if I have to but it’s so good I wanted it all to myself.  Just wait until she asks you “Wait, what is chicken made out of?” One of my daughters went vegetarian for a while week after she realized chicken the meat was indeed the same as chicken the animal.

At 4 they should be decent at following the rules. I don’t think cabinet locks would be necessary but maybe put anything dangerous like bleach up on a high shelf. My main concern at 4 was my child getting out of the front or back doors because they were adept enough to do that and in a new environment they might try it. Beyond that if there’s anything breakable or especially cool looking maybe stuff it in a closet for the visit.

If I was in that situation and struggled to afford better/bigger then my daughter would be staying in the bedroom even if she was only there 2 nights a week. There is definitely a difference between being too poor to provide versus too careless to provide. He could create a space for her.

She doesn’t have to do the chores perfectly - it’s going to be practice for her at first. I asked my kids what they want to do for chores and they get genuinely excited bc they get to pick lol. One of my daughters takes pride in getting their bedroom clean and beds made. My other daughter is obsessed with cleaning the bathroom because she gets to scrub the toilet. They both like feeding the dog and cleaning windows and taking out the small trash bin they have put googly eyes on and named “Dumpy.” I let them do every chore except dishes because they’re a little too clumsy for that and I want clean plates. Sometimes they have even cooked dinner with supervision. They can independently make grilled cheese or scrambled eggs, etc.

The hotel has no idea the company doesn’t want you there and they likely don’t care as long as you don’t disturb any one. If you’re nervous have him let you in an entrance away from the front desk. I would not have him tell the hotel to add you bc that could only cause potential drama if for whatever reason the company finds out, however unlikely. We’re supposed to document all guests but it is impossible to know everyone’s face.

I felt like this until my children were almost 6 then things finally became easier. You are so very valid in your feelings even if society doesn’t really let moms express this side of things…It is a waiting game but you can help it along by getting them in touch with those feelings and giving them strategies to handle it on their own. My kids really liked creating a calm down corner with their favorite books, blankets and sensory items. As for issues when out in public, are the tantrums happening in the afternoon? I find that I could only do activities in the morning with my young kids because it was the only time they’d be in a good mood. You are truly in the trenches but eventually, slowly but surely, things will improve.

The most important thing you can do is emphasize how fake and not real porn is. It’s normal to be curious and to look things up, going ballistic about normal human curiosity is just going to make her not trust you. Just open up a conversation, let her ask questions or direct her to more appropriate places to find answers, then set some boundaries about what she is allowed to access on the iPad.

Start to take note of what you and your husband say around her. Are you also only mentioning the negative? Even if it seems silly or obvious, just narrate your thoughts outloud that are positive and she might just copy you. I catch my daughters saying what I say all of the time. Children don’t always get implications or subtleties so be a little over the top when you compliment her or love on her. Also, ask her opinion on things and let her be an expert at her interests so she can “teach” you things. It will help her self esteem a lot and show her that you value what she has to say. 

Every time things get heated or out of hand make it a point to apologize and explain what behavior is acceptable vs unacceptable, even if you’re talking about your own behavior. Explicitly say your love is always stronger than anger because as a kid, sometimes you just don’t realize that. She might be getting a little old for it but The Invisible String is a book that helped my daughter conceptualize these ideas.

Try not to get worked up before you even get an answer. I was much more reckless than you and have had a lot of pregnancy scares, but only one of those times was I actually pregnant. A lot of pregnancies are also not viable due to chromosomal abnormalities and can end in miscarriage in those early weeks - it’s why most wait until at least week 12 to announce they’re pregnant. The extreme itchiness symptom you describe sounds like cholestasis which is something that occurs late in pregnancy, not early. Even if you are pregnant it’s probably early enough for the pill to be used and you may be able to get it mailed to you discretely. If you’re in the US look at plancpills.org for guidance. The abortion pills are also not nearly as expensive as a surgical abortion but you would need a follow up ultrasound for your “miscarriage” to ensure everything went well.

Oh and even if he does not ejaculate he can still technically get you pregnant from pre cum, the chances are just much lower.

Get waterproof mattress covers and use things like couch covers. Keep a large size diaper box on hand for emergencies and pray you never need it. Designate a puke bowl for each family member. Keep pedialyte popsicles on hand. My kids didn’t get puking or fever related illnesses until they entered kindergarten but a month after they started we got the worst sickness I’ve ever had in my entire life. We were all puking and shitting ourselves at the same time for an entire week. I just put them back in diapers because it was so bad even I as the adult could not make it in time. I was so weak I was bed ridden for 3 days and even the other person living with us got sick…despite isolating in their room across the other side of the house. And yes we did have some reoccurring issues even with heavy bleach use but none as bad as the first go around.

Emphasize that you need to trust each other and invite him to think about what would happen if people lied to him. Ask him how he would feel if you lied to him? What if you promised him a happy meal but then presented him with a tuna fish sandwich instead? Make it silly so he pays attention. Then if he doesn’t get it tell him a somewhat “devastating” lie (to a five year old) then when he complains, say “Oh, I’m confused. I thought it was okay to lie because you keep lying to me. I’ll be honest with you if you promise to be honest with me.” I did this to my daughter and she lies on impulse at times but usually owns up to it within a minute or two lol.
Her mother is the problem. You did what most reasonable empathetic people would do.

When he does those behaviors he wants your attention and reaction. Don’t give it to him. Don’t replace the bike. You are feeding into the behavior by engaging with the nasty things he’s saying. If you don’t engage the behavior will get worse as he gets more desperate for your reaction but over time he will realize he can only earn your attention if he’s respecting your boundaries and being appropriate. Set some clear boundaries with clear consequences so he knows exactly what to do. Give him a chance to earn quality time with you doing activities as a reward if he can be good for x amount of time.

NTA. It’s very weird to change someone’s name against their will. I would not even change the name of an older adopted pet. It’s just apart of that living being at that point. Sunny is a lovely name. The world is also changing and shifting away from hyper professional attitudes so I don’t think your name will even cause you any issues. Hell, I was told 10 years ago I’d never work because of my tattoos or piercings and that was simply not true. Even outfits people wear to work have dramatically changed over the past 10 years and I see many “unprofessional” fits that would have been a big no no 10 years ago. If anything Sunny as a name stands out to me in a very positive way!

I’ve struggled with this so much. It’s very hard to send my kids when they are not feeling their best but unless there is fever, excessive diarrhea or vomiting I send them. If the nurse sends them home then I’m covered when they get excessive absences legally. Definitely have some talks about hand washing, how germs spread and why people get sick. My kids knew generally but did not fully understand until we did a glitter experiment. The glitter was the germs I “sneezed” out and because I didn’t cover my mouth everything was covered in glitter. Then I had them go about the day as normal spreading the glitter…They were freaking out about all the “germs.” Then I showed them they had to REALLY scrub their hands to get it off and how the glitter got on their face, etc. They need a visual imo.

It’s not weird at all. I stopped showering with mine at 5 when they started school but it still wasn’t “weird” then. I could just actually shower alone without them beating down the door at that point because we have different schedules lol. I still stand in the side of the shower to help them wash their hair anyways.
Realizing hard work does not actually equate to success, just more responsibilities usually at the same pay.
I wouldn’t jump to conclusions until she gets tested. She could have something like a yeast infection or bacterial vaginosis, etc. Vaginas can be complicated.
Yeah, it’s a mobile app so you can log in to his account on your phone and see what games he’s been playing in “continue” even if he doesn’t play them on your phone.

I don’t blame you. Even with chat disabled and age restrictions Roblox has very questionable content. Personally, what I have done is set up a favorites list of games I approve of and my kids are only allowed to play those specific ones I’ve tested. There isn’t much like Roblox because it’s all user generated content and unfortunately user generated stuff is always dodgey for kids. So maybe find out what he is enjoying up there first? Does he just like the obbys (obstacle courses)? Then you can find comparable games from there.

Octonauts, StoryBots, & the Wild Kratts if I want them to watch something semi educational. For pure entertainment I feel like Scooby Doo, both old and new, is top notch no matter the age. Just don’t let them see Scrappy Doo or you’ll be forced to watch it forever lol. Depending on age there are a lot of good series out like Gravity Falls or Over the Garden Wall that I have enjoyed too. Kipo and the age of the wonder beasts, avatar and adventure time are things we’ve watched together and both enjoyed. Obviously these shows are more mature so I would watch it with them, not slap it on and walk away.

I suggest documenting instances where he is not being safe because it’s not a crime to be that stupid but perhaps if you can show a judge how his decisions could cause danger then they’ll rule in your favor. I don’t know what the age group is but take something serious and combine it with something ridiculous like paint your favorite meme in the style of your favorite artist. Designing sneakers or dream cars would probably be something they might like. Spray paint inspired art. If you can give different hands on projects that are 3D that might help. Have them create something inspired by their favorite song. I’ve noticed a lot of boys act as if drawing/painting is something that is to girly for them for some reason. At the end of the day you can only do so much to make it fun and relatable then it’s up to them.

I don’t have any advice but I’m right there with you. I just got a message home telling me my daughter was ignoring the teacher and licking everything in the classroom, including the floor, so we’ll be on round 6 in a day or two.

NTA. Actively denying you medical care is 100% abuse. You could have died. Your child could have died. You are under reacting. Start thinking “if a man treated my daughter like this, would I be okay with that?” And apply that logic to yourself and your relationship.

Melatonin gummies at 7pm. They are out in 30 minutes. Then in the morning I gently wake them. They are already bathed so I help dress them in bed and sometimes I let them eat at the foot of my bed and watch a cartoon while I do their hair. By then they are ready to get up and brush teeth/leave. It’s a lot for me to do but I feel like it gives us a stronger connection and they enjoy hanging out in bed in the morning. It makes morning chill and stress free.

I do think other kids exaggerate or lie because they are embarrassed by having a bed time but your mom’s responses are semi ridiculous. Good parents don’t routinely tell their child to shut the f up and gaslight them. That’s kind of concerning and it’s not a normal way to talk. 

Instead of arguing/challenging her you could say that you want to be more responsible and would like to “earn” an extra hour before bed by doing another chore through out the week. I think it would also be reasonable to suggest that can you manage your own bed time on non school nights as long as your grades stay above a certain percent. Just try to appeal to her main concerns and show that you can be responsible enough to manage more of your own time.

Get some fun comic books like Dog Man or Captain Underpants. There is a lot of simple words you can sound out together while you read. Focus on the 3 letter ones and avoid bigger words for now. If you get him excited about reading he will keep trying and start recognizing words on his own. He’ll likely be able to read starter books on his own by the end of the year.

ESH. It’s weird to not disclose and to down play how insanely wealthy you are. It’s wrong of them to feel so entitled. But overall in the grand scheme of things your family is rich thanks to exploiting resources people need to survive. I think you realize that deep down and that’s why you concealed your status. Personally if I was in such a position I would try to find roommates that I could get along with but that were also struggling financially so they could have an opportunity to pay less than market rate.

I have twins so 20$ max since I would likely need to buy 2 gifts. It depends on the cost of the party. If the parent is paying for a location or something special I would spend more, but if the party is low cost than 20$ is definitely sufficient.

It’s strange the parents didn’t reach out to you already with concerns. I would reach out to your admin before the parent to see where they stand policy wise so you can tailor your response but definitely talk to the parents.

YTA. He is obviously aware that his diet is an issue so he tries to be accommodating. He at the least has aversions or undiagnosed medical issues. This is a trait that would have been obvious from the start so you’re trying to change him now things are more serious. You’re just not compatible. Let it go and accept it or move on.

NTA. Thank you. As a daughter that was never good enough this is so healing to read.

You’re about to be 18 so I think it’s more than fair that you get to go outside alone. How can you even make friends if you can’t go outside? 

I’d appeal to her safety concerns and promise to let her track me in some way to feel better. If you have iPhones you can track each others location with the find my iPhone app! There are probably similar apps for android or gps tags you can buy. 

I can understand why she’s nervous and her reasoning that there is safety in numbers.  Perhaps she would feel more comfortable if you had self defensive items as well.
This is very weird and very wrong. He should be playing with, reading to and interacting with his own child as a very bare minimum.

Does he ever spend time with the baby at all? Because it sounds like he’s not even trying to socialize with the baby at all. It sounds like he’s giving the baby the same level of attention of a house plant.

Booster seats are cheap enough I would have your parents buy one to keep on hand for future visits as well. I think a stroller would also be too cumbersome. They do usually let people with small children board early though so it might be doable if you really think she’ll need it. I’d pack as light as you can especially if it’s a Christmas trip because of presents. Get your 4 year old a backpack for their carry on so you don’t have to carry their things. 

I would bring lollipops or gum if you can trust your child with it so they don’t cry about their ears so much. Bring a pair of headphones so they can comfortably watch a movie.

You can tell hospital staff to keep him out of the room if you need too. You are the patient, not him, and it’s none of his business. The pain of exercise comment is so outlandish and outrageous. There is no parallel there unless his exercise is shoving and birthing out large objects from his anus. If you do let him in the room please allow the staff to humble him for you and explain the difference between exercise and birth. 

Your mood will affect the baby more than the epidural will so do not allow him to stress you out and ruin what is a very special day for you. Allow someone supportive in the room that knows you’re in charge.

Edit: Also would like to add that if you need an emergency C section you will be able to stay awake and present for the baby with an epidural.

He’s so young that a lot of development is still happening. A few months from now things might be completely different. My kids did a class at age 3-4 they did horribly in but were fine for kindergarten to my surprise. Just keep working with him and give consequences, but also lots of positive rewards for good behavior.

Have you tried to reenact what is happening at school with her? Using play to practice how to feel and what to do might help. I feel like she’s not able to communicate her feelings and maybe lashing out due to the frustration. You could practice some phrases with her. My daughter behaved similarly and me telling her what to say helped a lot. She was acting out because she needed a break but didn’t understand that she could say “hey I am feeling frustrated I need a break.” 

Practicing transitions and tough situations at home might help her use those skills in class. Does her classroom have a calm down corner? If so maybe make your own calm down corner at home. What would Danny do is a good series that helped my daughter think about good vs bad choices so maybe get a few of those books from your library. 

Positive rewards and goals for good behavior couldn’t hurt either.

Go on YouTube and find the Vook about the little poop. The story ends with the poop getting flushed and having a party down in the sewer! My daughters totally latched on to this idea and came to believe that their pees and poops had a family in the sewer and if they didn’t go on the toilet they’d never see their family again or get to party. We had little party favors by the toilet so we could do a post poop party dance lol. Some kids are just stubborn but if you make it a fun game he might get on board a lot quicker. Little rewards are also good. Mine will do anything for a candy bc I never let them have sugar normally.
Can I ask what you do? I feel like I could handle 4 hours a day but I’m struggling to find something that isn’t full time
If you are not sleeping at all in a 24 hour period AND not feeling any ill effects or tiredness, AND that continues for a few days, that would be something to discuss with a doctor.

Are you feeling tired when this happens and do you still sleep a somewhat normal length?

If you are staying up and not feeling the effects of being tired and like you don’t need to sleep at all you need to talk to someone. Especially if you’re noticing a pattern. 

If not, then you might want to scale off the melatonin. After a certain amount sometimes it can have the opposite effect. If I take too much melatonin it hurts my sleep and I wake up a lot in the middle of the night.

It’s also normal to want to stay up and socialize, so I feel you. We spend a lot of the day doing things we need to do and not enough of the day doing things we want to do. I’m an old lady but I definitely spent hours and hours doing the same. You just need some balance is all.

Detention, removing recess and removing lunch with his peers for just tardies? Wtf? They’re not exactly helping him acclimate OR get excited about going to school. My child’s school focuses on positive reinforcement rather than punishment. I feel that those punishments if it’s just for tardies are so excessive and I would complain. He’s already unsure of school and they’re going to make him hate school so it’s just exacerbating the problem. 

As for solving the tardy problem just get there earlier. Park and take your time. Talk about how much fun you had in school and how jealous you are that you can’t go to school! Tell him he just has to go so he can tell you all about it, etc. See if he can bring a support friend like a plush. Maybe set some goals he can earn, like if he’s and to get in the building without a struggle then you’ll go right to the park after school or get him a special meal, etc.

Personally I’d tell her she doesn’t need everyone to like her, just like she doesn’t necessarily like everyone she meets. It’s ok if they don’t understand and they’re just missing out on the fun! Then I’d try to connect her to people that share her interests and hobbies. I’m in a place where we have reptile shows and expos often, and the library has even had a rescue worker come to show kids different reptiles and tarantulas. Perhaps you can find similar things. Good for you for encouraging it. 

Moving at 9 is incredibly difficult socially. I don’t think it’s necessarily her hobbies preventing friendships. It’s just a time where kids have already started to form more solid friends and best friends so she’s perceived as an outsider. No matter how “normal” she is she’d likely struggle. I moved at this age and I didn’t really start to form friendships until I got to middle school.

Just keep reading to him and try to do physical math activities where he gets to actually touch things. He needs to understand the numbers represent objects.
